abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.
hook: Cube projections have maximal entropy along the diagonal-like directions, proved for dimensions 150 and up
summary: The paper proves that when a uniform cube is projected onto a line, the result is most spread out (highest differential entropy) when all coordinates of the direction have equal size. This settles a conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz, but only for dimensions n of at least 150. Lower dimensions remain open.
title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
